image.name: Catalyst Old River Hydroelectric Limited Partnership
aliases: Sidney A. Murray Jr. Hydroelectric Station
image.description: Catalyst Old River Hydroelectric Limited Partnership owns and operates the 192 MW Sidney A. Murray Jr. Hydroelectric Station on a diversion of the Mississippi River near Vidalia, Louisiana. The run-of-river facility entered service in 1990 and sells power to an Entergy utility and the Town of Vidalia under long-term arrangements extending through 2031. Brookfield Renewable affiliates hold the 75% economic balance and the managing/control position. ArcLight Capital Partners holds the remaining 25% through ArcLight Renewable Infrastructure Fund SM SPV, L.P., which acquired the interest from ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V on July 8, 2021. The project company is the single PortCo; its upstream holdcos, co-licensee and lenders are not separate owners.

image.name: Electrada
image.description: Electrada, LLC was a U.S. commercial fleet-charging platform that financed, owned and managed charging infrastructure under charging-as-a-service arrangements. Launched in 2020 and headquartered in Cincinnati, the company served commercial, institutional and public fleets through no-upfront-capex infrastructure and energy-management contracts. BlackRock Climate Infrastructure backed Electrada beginning in 2021, but the exact fund, vehicle and stake were not publicly disclosed. On April 20, 2026, Current Trucking acquired Electrada's operating, construction and development assets, more than 30 sites, customer agreements and select personnel. On June 17, 2026, Inspiration Mobility acquired select remaining assets, team, pipeline, depot-development capability, energy software and intellectual property. Those transactions ended Electrada as a standalone operating platform; neither buyer is treated as a full legal successor and no GIP ownership period exists.

image.name: TXNM Energy
image.description: TXNM Energy, Inc. is the Albuquerque, New Mexico-based public holding company above regulated electric utilities Public Service Company of New Mexico and Texas-New Mexico Power. The platform serves residential, commercial and industrial customers in New Mexico and Texas through rate-regulated generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure. The corporation was incorporated in 2000, established its holding-company structure in 2001 and changed its name from PNM Resources to TXNM Energy in August 2024. Blackstone Infrastructure signed an agreement on May 19, 2025 to acquire 100% of TXNM. A separate $400 million PIPE for eight million shares closed on June 2, 2025, but a New Mexico order caused those shares to be cancelled and the investment repaid on July 22, 2026. TXNM therefore remains publicly owned while the take-private remains signed and pending regulatory approvals. No specific final Blackstone fund allocation or legal closing date is publicly disclosed.

image.name: American Roads
image.description: American Roads owns and operates four tolled transportation assets: the American side of the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel and three Alabama toll bridges. The platform serves passenger and commercial traffic and John Laing reports approximately seven million annual trips. DIF Infrastructure V acquired 100% of American Roads in July 2018. CVC DIF signed the sale to John Laing in February 2026, and John Laing announced financial close on April 28, 2026 and now reports 100% ownership. The exact legal closing date and acquiring SPV are not publicly disclosed. The Foley Beach Express Bridge exited the platform in May 2024 and is not a current asset. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Prince George's County Blueprint Schools Program (Phase One)
aliases: Prince George's County Education & Community Partners, LLC
image.description: Prince George's County Blueprint Schools Program (Phase One) is an availability-based DBFM concession covering six public schools in Prince George's County, Maryland through Prince George's County Education & Community Partners, LLC. The ProjectCo reached financial close on December 18, 2020 with Fengate-controlled entities holding 75% and Gilbane Development holding 25%. Five middle schools opened in August 2023 and Colin L. Powell K-8 Academy opened in November 2023; lifecycle and facilities-management services continue under a term ending June 30, 2053. BBGI acquired 100% from the Fengate and Gilbane vehicles in February 2026 and remains the current owner; BCI's ownership of BBGI is upstream and is not added as a separate ProjectCo owner. Phase Two is a distinct project. No later sale, concession termination or signed ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.name: Cambrian Innovation
image.subsector: Industrial water reuse and wastewater treatment
image.description: Cambrian Innovation, Inc. develops, owns and operates distributed industrial wastewater treatment, water-reuse and energy-recovery infrastructure through service-based Water-Energy Purchase Agreement structures. Pennybacker-affiliated funds acquired Cambrian on November 16, 2023 and committed up to US$200 million of growth equity; current company materials continue to identify Pennybacker as the corporate owner. Generate Capital's earlier participation concerned project-level WEPA financing and jointly owned project vehicles beginning in 2015, not current corporate ownership, and its exact project-SPV stake and exit date were not publicly disclosed. Cambrian announced a US$150 million ING credit facility in June 2025 to expand its active infrastructure portfolio; that facility is debt. No later corporate sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.name: Pine Gate Renewables
image.description: Pine Gate Renewables was a U.S. developer and owner-operator of utility-scale solar and storage projects. Founded in 2016, it received a US$500 million growth-and-asset financing commitment from Generate Capital in 2022 and a US$650 million investment involving Generate, HOOPP and HESTA in 2024. Pine Gate entered Chapter 11 in November 2025. Five sale transactions transferred development, operations and project packages between January and April 2026; the liquidation plan became effective on April 22, 2026 and cancelled all existing equity. The historical integrated-platform record is therefore realized. MorningSky Power, ACT Power Services and the separate project-buyer businesses are not treated as continuations of this record.
